applicability: Applies to expressions given as an ordered list of integer operands (length 1..8, each in [-10,20]) and a list of binary operators from '+','-','*' with exactly len(operands)-1 entries, where the task is to count distinct values over all full parenthesizations preserving operand and operator order. Does not handle other operators, unary operators, reordering, non-integer operands, or expressions outside the stated bounds; such inputs are rejected with ValueError.
description: Interval dynamic programming over the original operand/operator sequence. dp[i][j] holds the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing operands[i..j] with operators[i..j-1]. Base case dp[i][i]={operands[i]}. For each interval length, each split k combines every value from dp[i][k] and dp[k+1][j] via operators[k] (+, -, *), inserting into dp[i][j]. The answer is the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. No subexpression is pre-collapsed, so all Catalan-many parenthesizations are covered and duplicates are removed by set semantics. Exact Python integer arithmetic is used. Inputs are validated against the schema (list lengths, integer operands in [-10,20], operators in {+,-,*}, booleans rejected); malformed inputs raise ValueError. Uncertainty: assumes 'fully parenthesize' means all binary tree groupings preserving order, which matches the stated problems; complexity is O(n^3 * S^2) with small n (<=8).
